question: Explain the differential diagnosis boundary for DIS-008 using registered Wiki evidence.
answer: 猪流行性腹泻；authority_supported_ped_boundary_or_fact；WOAH identifies PED as a non-zoonotic viral disease of pigs caused by a coronavirus and characterised by watery diarrhoea and weight loss. [source=A1-WOAH-PED rule=RC-CITATION-001 fact=DIS008-WEB-001-woah-nonzoonotic-coronavirus page=wiki/diseases/DIS-008-porcine-epidemic-diarrhea-virus.md]; 猪流行性腹泻；authority_supported_ped_boundary_or_fact；WOAH states that PED affects pigs of all ages but is most severe in neonatal piglets, with morbidity and mortality reaching up to 100% and mortality decreasing as age increases. [source=A1-WOAH-PED rule=RC-CITATION-001 fact=DIS008-WEB-002-woah-age-morbidity-mortality page=wiki/diseases/DIS-008-porcine-epidemic-diarrhea-virus.md]; 猪流行性腹泻；authority_supported_ped_boundary_or_fact；WOAH states that PED is mainly transmitted by the faecal-oral route and that prevention and management control focus on strict biosecurity and early detection. [source=A1-WOAH-PED rule=RC-CITATION-001 fact=DIS008-WEB-003-woah-fecal-oral-biosecurity-early-detection page=wiki/diseases/DIS-008-porcine-epidemic-diarrhea-virus.md]; 猪流行性腹泻；authority_supported_ped_boundary_or_fact；WOAH states that PED is clinically similar to other forms of porcine gastroenteritis and that there is no specific treatment; this supports diagnostic and treatment-boundary use only. [source=A1-WOAH-PED rule=RC-CITATION-001 fact=DIS008-WEB-004-woah-clinical-similarity-no-specific-treatment page=wiki/diseases/DIS-008-porcine-epidemic-diarrhea-virus.md]
